steps.user_message: I'm preparing my 2024 taxes and could use your help. Situation: married filing jointly, Seattle WA. W-2 from Acme Corp: $82,350. Side income: $11,200 from web design (3 clients). Interest $2,340 (Chase savings), dividends $550 (Interactive Brokers). Home office: 155 sq ft, rent $1,820/month, apartment 680 sq ft. Deductions: student loan interest $4,400 (Sallie Mae, 2019–2020); charity $2,000 to Boston Medical Center (donation, have receipt) with receipt; unreimbursed expenses $720. Can you help me figure out deductions, standard vs itemized, and home office treatment—and which forms to use?
steps.expected_behavior: Agent should help with tax-related questions based on available information.
steps.agent_response:
Here’s a concise plan for your 2024 return based on what you shared.

Bottom line recommendations
- Standard vs itemized: Take the standard deduction (MFJ 2024 = $29,200). Your likely itemized deductions are far lower (mainly $2,000 charity; WA has no state income tax, and sales tax via IRS tables would still leave you well below $29,200).
- Student loan interest: Deduct $2,500 (max allowed; your income is well under the 2024 MFJ phaseout).
- Home office: Use the actual-expense method for your Schedule C. Based on rent alone, the deduction is much larger than the simplified method.

Key calculations (estimates)
- Home office
  - Office size: 155 sq ft; home: 680 sq ft → business use 22.8%.
  - Rent: $1,820 × 12 = $21,840.
  - Actual-method deduction: 22.8% × $21,840 ≈ $4,978. Simplified method would be 155 × $5 = $775.
- Side business (Schedule C)
  - Net profit if $720 are business expenses: $11,200 − $4,978 − $720 ≈ $5,502.
  - Self-employment tax (Schedule SE): ≈ $779; above-the-line SE tax deduction ≈ $389.
  - QBI deduction (Form 8995): ≈ 20% of qualified business income (roughly $1,000 based on the above).
- Other income
  - W-2 wages: $82,350
  - Interest: $2,340 (triggers Schedule B because > $1,500)
  - Dividends: $550 (also listed on Schedule B)
- AGI snapshot (if $720 are business expenses and using actual home office): 
  - AGI before adjustments ≈ $90,742; minus $2,500 (student loan interest) and ≈$389 (half SE tax) → ≈ $87,853.
  - Taxable income ≈ $87,853 − $29,200 (standard) − ≈$1,022 (QBI) ≈ $57,600. This is just to illustrate why standard deduction is best; final numbers depend on exact expenses and forms.

Which forms to use
- Form 1040
- Schedule 1: Adjustments (student loan interest; half SE tax)
- Schedule B: Interest and dividends (interest exceeds $1,500)
- Schedule C: Side business income and expenses
- Schedule SE: Self-employment tax
- Home office:
  - Form 8829 if you use the actual-expense method (recommended here)
  - If you choose the simplified method instead, claim it directly on Schedule C line for home office (no Form 8829)
- Form 8995: Qualified Business Income deduction
- You’ll also report info from:
  - W-2 from Acme
  - 1099-NEC from any client(s) who issued one (report the income even if you didn’t receive 1099s)
  - 1099-INT (Chase) and 1099-DIV (Interactive Brokers)
  - 1098-E (student loan interest) if issued

Notes and assumptions to confirm
- The $720 “unreimbursed expenses”: If they’re for your side web-design business, they go on Schedule C. If they’re W-2 job expenses, they’re generally not deductible for 2024.
- Home office qualifies only if used exclusively and regularly for the business, and it’s your principal place for admin/management (or where you meet clients).
- If you have other home costs (internet, utilities, renter’s insurance), the actual-expense method could increase your home office deduction further.
- Charitable gifts: Keep the receipt. They only reduce tax if you itemize; with standard deduction, there’s no separate federal write-off.

Want me to:
- Prepare a clean summary you can email to your CPA, or
- Draft an email to your spouse/records with these figures and a document checklist?
